title: EGO to SIM to PhiAgent fixed third-person tabletop replay

sim_rendering.classification: Constrained target-camera geometric replay; not a contact-dynamics simulation
rasterized_geometry: Synthetic static room, table, mat, and partitions
Fixed-length arm segments and shared torso mesh
Tracked alarm-clock and cylinder object meshes
sim_rendering.visibility: Per-pixel nvdiffrast depth buffers compose static and dynamic meshes from the fixed target camera
constraints: Source-world actor origin is independent of the render camera
Upper-arm and forearm lengths remain constant
Both arms connect to one stable shared torso
Reviewed grasp intervals stabilize relative hand/object geometry
Object persistence and an upright-clock prior are imposed for this scene

phiagent_generation.input: Reviewed target-camera SIM, source appearance evidence, and scene/action prompt
phiagent_generation.generator: H3 Ref2VA path with PhiAgent review and repair orchestration
phiagent_generation.timing_repair: Monotone C1 PCHIP nearest-frame selection; no optical-flow synthesis or new H3/SIM generation

observations: All panel labels remain fixed and contain no experiment version numbers.
The clock, small blue cylinder, and tall cylinder remain identifiable through the sequence.
The fixed third-person camera, background, torso, arms, and action order remain visually continuous.

implemented: Consumed-output numerical gates and bounded temporary-memory statistics
In-process multi-request resident H3 worker with independent cache epochs
Cooperative same-NUMA four-GPU UUID selection and leases
not_claimed: Matched real-H3 warm-request speedup for the resident/same-NUMA path

limitations: One historical real tabletop scene; no additional-scene end-to-end acceptance
Not unattended raw-RGB calibration or a built-in autonomous VLM
Not exact 3-D contact, force closure, collision certification, or real-robot execution
Nearest-frame timing repair can introduce visible cadence changes
The three-panel delivery is a lossy H.264 encode, not pixel-identical preservation
